Speaking Skills & Effective Meetings

The 7 C's of Communication, Meeting Governance & The 10-Point Planning Audit

Academic Lead:Mrs. Ishara Raviharee Weerasinghe(Senior Lecturer in English | Lecturer In Charge)
SLIIT City Uni • Professional Skills Assessment Standard
Curriculum Overview & Context

Explores the 7 C's of executive verbal delivery and examines meeting governance types. Provides the 10-point planning audit checklist to eliminate corporate meeting bloat and enforce timekeeping discipline.

Core Competencies & Learning Objectives

  • →Apply the 7 C's of Executive Communication across verbal presentations and meetings.
  • →Distinguish between meeting typologies: Agile Standups, Customer Negotiations, Board Meetings, AGMs, and EGMs.
  • →Execute the 10-point meeting planning checklist to ensure strict outcome-oriented facilitation.
  • →Master the role of Chairperson as diplomatic referee: moderating dominant voices and drawing out quiet contributors.

The 7 C's of Executive Communication

The Universal Standard for Verbal & Written Clarity

Communication failure in engineering teams is rarely technical; it is almost always a breakdown in clarity, precision, or courtesy. The 7 C's provide an actionable filter for every spoken or written exchange.

1. Clear:Unambiguous message with simple language, free from confusing corporate jargon or obscure acronyms.
2. Concise:Economical with the listener's time; sticking strictly to the point without filler or circular explanations.
3. Concrete:Supported by solid facts, exact data, and verifiable metrics rather than vague abstractions.
4. Correct:Accurate information, proper grammar, verified technical statistics, and appropriate register.
5. Coherent:Logically structured with smooth transitions, ensuring each idea naturally connects to the next.
6. Complete:Contains all required details, deadlines, and context so the receiver can act without requesting clarification.
7. Courteous:Respectful, empathetic, professional tone that acknowledges the listener's perspective and time.

Meeting Typologies & Governance

Matching Structure to Strategic Purpose

Meetings represent a massive expenditure of organizational capital. Ineffective meetings waste thousands of developer hours each month. Understanding the legal and operational structure of meetings ensures disciplined execution.

Meeting ClassificationFrequency / ScopeGovernance Rules & Formal Protocols
Agile Standup / Sprint SyncDaily (15 mins)Strict timebox; three questions: What was completed? What is next? What blockers exist?
Customer / Client NegotiationAd-hoc / Milestone-drivenContractual alignment, value consensus, documented scope bounds, formal minutes.
Board MeetingMonthly / QuarterlyExecutive directors; legal fiduciary oversight, corporate governance, strategic capital allocation.
AGM (Annual General Meeting)Mandatory AnnuallyOpen to all shareholders; financial statement approvals, board elections, statutory voting.
EGM (Extraordinary General Meeting)Emergency / Special crisisConvened under company law for urgent matters requiring immediate shareholder vote.

The 10-Point Meeting Planning Checklist

Eliminating Waste and Enforcing Accountability

A successful meeting begins 48 hours before anyone enters the conference room and finishes only when action minutes are verified and delivered.

1. Explicit Purpose:Define clear objectives; if the outcome can be achieved via an email, cancel the meeting.
2. Timed Agenda:Circulate an agenda with exact minute allocations at least 48 hours in advance.
3. Curated Attendees:Invite only decision-makers and vital contributors; eliminate spectator bloat.
4. Optimized Environment:Maintain a cool ambient room temperature (cooler rooms promote mental alertness and combat drowsiness).
5. Technology AV Check:Pre-test projectors, video conferencing links, and screen sharing 10 minutes prior.
6. Chairperson as Referee:Diplomatically rein in dominant talkers and actively invite insights from quiet team members.
7. Punctual Discipline:Start strictly on time (never wait for latecomers) and end at or before the scheduled time.
8. Action-Oriented Minutes:Record explicit decisions, assigned owners, and agreed deadlines rather than conversational transcripts.
9. Immediate Distribution:Circulate summary minutes and task matrices within 24 hours of meeting completion.
10. Follow-up Accountability:Verify that assignees execute agreed action items prior to the next scheduled sync.
The Chairperson's Golden Rule
“A great chairperson is like a diplomatic sports referee: they do not dominate the game; they ensure fair participation, keep the ball moving forward, and penalize time-wasting.”
— Meeting Governance Protocol
Executive Governance Tool • 10-Point Audit

Meeting Preparation & Facilitation Audit

Audit Progress3 of 10 Complete (30%)
30%

Critical Environmental Protocol (Point 4): Cool Room Temperature

Academic research in conference management confirms that keeping meeting rooms noticeably cool prevents post-lunch lethargy, elevates oxygen delivery, and keeps participants mentally alert during high-stakes deliberations.

#01Pre-Meeting

Explicit Purpose & Desired Outcome

Establish non-negotiable deliverables. If the outcome can be achieved via an email, cancel the meeting immediately.

Rule: Clarity of purpose eliminates 80% of unnecessary corporate meetings.

#02Pre-Meeting

Strictly Timed Agenda (48h Advance)

Circulate a structured agenda with minute-by-minute timeboxing at least 48 hours prior to meeting kickoff.

Rule: Never open a meeting without an advance agenda.

#03Pre-Meeting

Essential Participant Curation

Invite only decision-makers and key technical contributors. Eliminate spectator bloat.

Rule: Amazon 2-pizza rule: smaller meetings yield exponentially higher decision velocity.

#04Pre-Meeting

Room Environment & Temperature Optimization

Maintain a cool ambient room temperature (cooler environments prevent carbon dioxide lethargy and sustain mental sharpness).

Rule: Overheated rooms cause 40% reduction in attendee cognitive attention.

#05Pre-Meeting

Technology & AV Pre-Testing

Test video links, audio mics, and screen sharing 10 minutes prior to prevent wasted start time.

Rule: Fumbling with cables communicates amateur preparation.

#06In-Meeting

Chairperson as Diplomatic Referee

The chairperson moderates dominant speakers and deliberately draws out insights from quieter participants.

Rule: A great chairperson facilitates without dominating.

#07In-Meeting

Punctual Timekeeping Discipline

Start strictly on the dot (never wait for latecomers) and end at or before the scheduled conclusion.

Rule: Starting late rewards tardiness and penalizes punctual professionals.

#08In-Meeting

Action-Oriented Decision Recording

Capture explicit decisions, assigned task owners, and deadline commitments rather than transcript ramblings.

Rule: Focus on WHO does WHAT by WHEN.

#09Post-Meeting

Immediate Minutes Distribution (<24h)

Circulate concise action minutes and the accountability matrix within 24 hours while memory is fresh.

Rule: Unrecorded decisions are rarely executed.

#10Post-Meeting

Follow-Up Accountability Verification

Verify that assigned task owners execute agreed deliverables prior to the subsequent review.

Rule: Accountability closes the operational feedback loop.

Chapter 05 Experiential Synthesis/Teran Rathnayake (SA25610122)/SLIIT City Uni

Connecting Theory to Practice: Undergraduate & Developer

Reflective analysis connecting Speaking Skills & Effective Meetings to coursework at SLIIT City Uni, software engineering projects (LA'CEDRA, TechMart, ApPoint), digital systems at LA'CEDRA, and collaborative teamwork.

01. Meaning & Conceptual Core

Executive speaking skills and meeting governance involve the disciplined delivery of verbal messages and the structured moderation of organizational syncs to eliminate operational drift, respect collective time, and achieve decisive consensus. It pairs the 7 C's of Communication with strict meeting typologies, timed agendas, and parliamentary minutes.

02. Key Theoretical Concepts Acquired
→The 7 C's of Executive Communication: Clear, Concise, Concrete, Correct, Coherent, Complete, and Courteous.
→Meeting Typology & Governance: Internal Agile Syncs (standups, retrospectives), Client Negotiations, and Executive Governance (Board Meetings, AGMs).
→The 10-Point Meeting Planning Checklist: Clear purpose, timed agenda circulated 48h prior, participant curation, environment optimization, tech testing, timekeeping, minutes, and accountability follow-up.
→Chairperson as Diplomatic Referee: Moderating dominant participants, drawing out introverted developers, and preventing tangent drift.
→Meeting Minutes Protocol: Formally recording decisions, assigned owners, and hard delivery deadlines within 24 hours.
IT//EQ
03. Industry Imperative — Why This Matters in Tech

The technology sector suffers chronically from 'meeting fatigue' and unproductive daily syncs where hours are lost to unstructured technical debates. Engineers who master concise public speaking and structured meeting facilitation keep sprint velocity high, prevent miscommunication between technical and business teams, and command leadership respect.
